newsitem.title: USA: Sprint Q2 net slightly below consensus.
newsitem.headline: Sprint Q2 net slightly below consensus.

text.p: Sprint Corp said on Thursday its second quarter results were driven by a double-digit growth rate in call volumes in long distance and a local access line growth rate at the top of the industry.

Sprint said it had net income of $256 million, or 59 cents per share, after a litigation settlement charge of $20 million pre-tax, or 3 cents per share after-tax, compared to $317 million, or 73 cents per share, in the second quarter of 1996.
The First Call consensus earnings estimate for the second quarter was for earnings of 63 cents per share.
The company posted a 5.8 percent increase in revenues to $3.68 billion from $3.48 billion in the second quarter.
Long distance division revenues rose 8.1 percent to $2.2 billion, reflecting a 15 percent increase in minutes of use, the industry's standard measure of network calling volumes.
The growth came despite increases in Sprint's bad debt provision, a tougher pricing environment and a very strong second quarter last year, the company said.
Local phone revenue gained 5.1 percent during the second quarter to $1.35 billion from $1.28 billion in last year's second quarter.
Access lines grew 5.6 percent to 7.3 million, which it said it expected to be among the best growth rates in the industry.

William Esrey, Sprint's chairman and chief executive officer, said that "Sprint's Long Distance Division continues to record strong volume and revenue growth rates, which we expect will reflect continued market share growth."

Esrey said the local telecoms unit will announce Thursday that local service customers in 19 states served by the division will be able to purchase a full range of Sprint's long distance, wireless, Internet and local products with one telephone call beginning in 1998.
Currently, the local companies primarily sell local service products, not the larger bundle of offerings.
The 1997 net income includes after-tax losses of 29 cents per share from joint ventures and emerging businesses, compared to 12 cents per share a year ago.

The 29 cents figure is made up of 5 cents per share of losses from its Global One international venture and by 19 cents of losses from construction of the Sprint PCS cellular network, of which it is a 40 percent owner.
It said it had a 10.3 percent increase in core business operating income to $653 million, excluding a legal charge of $20 million, from $592 million in the year ago quarter.
The company said income from core operations rose 8.2 percent to $398 million, or 91 cents per share, from $368 million, or 85 cents per share, a year ago.
Core results exclude the impact from joint ventures and emerging businesses and the nonrecurring $20 million charge.
Sprint said its combined frame relay, ATM and Internet protocol data services revenues from large business customers increased nearly 80 percent in the second quarter versus a year ago.

In the wholesale market, in which Sprint sells spare network capacity to other carriers, the company said it won several new accounts with revenue and volume growth rising more than 33 percent compared to a year ago.

Revenues in Sprint's product distribution and directory publishing businesses were $364 million in the second quarter, up 15.8 percent from $315 million in the second quarter of last year due to higher sales to affiliates.
((-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1712))
